## What this deck is {#what-this-is}

A fixture. Every slide here exists to give the geometry tests something
real to measure: prose that spans the content frame, mathematics that KaTeX
must lay out, tables, images, vertical stacks, and the uncounted slides that
Reveal hides from `getSlides()`.

- It is deliberately wordy, because a layout assertion needs a widest block
- It is deliberately long, because the overview grid needs more than twenty cards
- It is deliberately varied, because a preview must match its live slide

## The authored canvas {#authored-canvas}

The outer stage is the one public coordinate system. Live display, overview
previews and printed pages all share it, and the fit transform only ever
shrinks the authored page to meet the viewport it happens to land on.

Reveal itself runs embedded inside an inset content frame and does no scaling
of its own, which is what keeps ink coordinates stable across devices.

## A first equation {#first-equation}

For a random variable $X$ with density $f$, the expectation is

$$ \mathbb{E}[X] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x f(x) \, \mathrm{d}x $$

and the variance follows from it as

$$ \operatorname{Var}(X) = \mathbb{E}[X^2] - \left(\mathbb{E}[X]\right)^2 . $$

## Accents and operators {#accents}

$$ \hat{\beta} = \left(\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{X}\right)^{-1}\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{y} $$

$$ \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i, \qquad \tilde{\mu} = \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\mu} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_i - \mu)^2 $$

## A table of moments {#moments-table}

| Distribution | Mean | Variance |
|--------------|------|----------|
| Bernoulli    | p    | p(1-p)   |
| Binomial     | np   | np(1-p)  |
| Poisson      | lam  | lam      |
| Exponential  | 1/lam | 1/lam^2 |
| Normal       | mu   | sigma^2  |

## Prose that fills the frame {#wide-prose}

This paragraph exists so that the widest measurable block on the slide is a
genuine run of text rather than a heading, because the layout assertions check
that real prose spans a substantial fraction of the content frame rather than
collapsing into a corner when the authored units fail to reach the content.

## Quotations {#quotation}

> All models are wrong, but some are useful.

The line above is a blockquote, which the theme styles differently from body
text and which therefore exercises a separate path through the stylesheet.

## Emphasis and links {#emphasis}

Text can be *emphasised*, **strongly emphasised**, or turned into a
[link](https://quarto.org) whose colour comes from the theme rather than the
browser default.

## A longer argument {#longer-argument}

When a deck is authored at a fixed size and shrunk to fit, every length inside
it is stable. That is the property the tests here defend: a heading is the same
number of authored units wide on a laptop, a projector and a tablet, and the
only thing that changes between them is the single scale factor applied to the
whole page.

## Numbered steps {#numbered-steps}

1. Author the page at a fixed size
2. Measure the viewport
3. Apply one uniform transform
4. Never scale anything else

## Small print {#small-print}

::: {.small}
Smaller text is used for asides and attributions. It still has to sit inside
the content frame and still has to appear in an overview preview.
:::

## Definitions {#definitions}

A *sample space* is the set of outcomes an experiment can produce. An *event*
is any subset of that set, and a *probability measure* assigns each event a
number between zero and one in a way that is countably additive.
